def components(g):
    h,w=len(g),len(g[0]); seen=set(); out=[]
    for r in range(h):
      for c in range(w):
        if (r,c) in seen: continue
        col=g[r][c]; q=[(r,c)]; seen.add((r,c)); cells=[]
        while q:
          x,y=q.pop(); cells.append((x,y))
          for a,b in ((x-1,y),(x+1,y),(x,y-1),(x,y+1)):
            if 0<=a<h and 0<=b<w and (a,b) not in seen and g[a][b]==col:
              seen.add((a,b)); q.append((a,b))
        out.append((col,cells))
    return out

def transform(grid):
    g=[row[:] for row in grid]
    bg=Counter(v for row in g for v in row).most_common(1)[0][0]
    cs=[(col,cells) for col,cells in components(g) if col!=bg]
    # The instruction is the conspicuous, connected L made of a single color.
    markers=[]
    for col,cells in cs:
      rs=[r for r,c in cells]; ys=[c for r,c in cells]
      hh=max(rs)-min(rs)+1; ww=max(ys)-min(ys)+1
      if len(cells)>=7 and hh>=3 and ww>=3 and len(cells)<hh+ww:
        markers.append((len(cells),col,cells))
    if not markers: return g
    _, ink, _=max(markers)
    # Recolor the smaller L-shaped object, the scaled instance of the instruction.
    for col,cells in cs:
      if col==ink or len(cells)<3: continue
      rs=[r for r,c in cells]; ys=[c for r,c in cells]

        for r,c in cells: g[r][c]=ink
        break
    return g
